server.title: Celesto Cloud Computers
server.description: Help agents create persistent Celesto Cloud computers, inspect their resources and state, run shell commands, start or stop them, delete them, and manage public HTTP ports.

protocolMetadata.instructions: Help agents create persistent Celesto Cloud computers, inspect their resources and state, run shell commands, start or stop them, delete them, and manage public HTTP ports. These tools manage Celesto Cloud computers for the account authenticated by this request. They do not manage computers on this server's machine.

tool.name: cloud_computer_create
tool.title: Create Cloud Computer
tool.description:
Create a persistent Cloud computer.

Use a new key per computer and reuse it on retries. Ask the user which size_id to use before calling; without one the call is refused and lists the sizes available on this account. Returns name (the created or reused computer id), provider, and state after the computer reaches running. Use that name in subsequent computer tools.

size_id.description: User-chosen CPU and RAM allocation for the new computer. Availability depends on the account's plan.

template_id.description: What the computer starts with. Defaults to scratch, a bare Ubuntu without Python or Node.js. coding-agent adds Python, Node.js, Git and common build tools.

idempotency_key.description: Client-chosen identity for this creation. Reuse it with the same size and template on retries; use a new key for another computer.

name.description: Id of the created (or idempotently reused) computer.

state.description: Lifecycle state after the operation (running, stopped, or deleted).

tool.description: List non-deleted Celesto Cloud computers in the authenticated organization. Returns provider, computers (computer_id and current status), the applied limit, and possibly_truncated. tool.name: cloud_computer_exec
tool.title: Run Command on Cloud Computer
tool.description: Run a shell command on a running Celesto Cloud computer and return stdout, stderr, and exit_code. Commands can modify or delete files, launch processes, and contact external services; repeating a call executes the command again. Output may be truncated, as indicated by stdout_truncated and stderr_truncated. If the MCP request times out, the command may still be running and its output cannot be recovered from that call; check before retrying.

tool.name: cloud_computer_port_publish
tool.title: Publish Cloud Computer Port
tool.description: Expose an HTTP application on a running Celesto Cloud computer through a public URL. Run the application on the guest port for the URL to serve traffic. Anyone with the URL can reach it, so protect sensitive endpoints in the application. Returns name, provider, route id, computer_id, port, url, status, and created_at. The url identifies the public route and status reports its publication state. Publishing an already-published port reuses its route.

tool.name: cloud_computer_port_list
tool.title: List Cloud Computer Ports
tool.description: List public HTTP routes for a Celesto Cloud computer, including suspended routes and publication changes. Returns name, provider, and ports; each port has id, computer_id, guest port, public url, status, and created_at. Check status before using a URL: only published routes are enabled, and the application must be listening. An empty ports array means there are no active route records.

tool.name: cloud_computer_port_unpublish
tool.title: Unpublish Cloud Computer Port
tool.description: Remove a public HTTP route from a Celesto Cloud computer; it does not stop the application inside the computer. Queues removal and returns the route's current status, which may be unpublishing while removal is in progress. Once removal completes, the public URL stops forwarding requests. If no active route exists, returns status=unpublished with no URL.

_published_faq.name: How do I add Celesto Cloud Computers to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor?

acceptedAnswer.text: Add Celesto Cloud Computers to Claude, ChatGPT, or Cursor by connecting its remote MCP URL in each client's MCP settings. In Claude, add a custom connector. In ChatGPT, add an MCP app. In Cursor, add an MCP server under Settings. The MCP URL is https://mcp.celesto.ai/mcp.

_published_faq.name: Is Celesto Cloud Computers MCP ready for ChatGPT and Claude?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Celesto Cloud Computers scores 100/100 on Manufact's MCP publishing checklist. The scan meets ChatGPT publishing checks and meets Claude publishing checks. Passing these checks does not guarantee marketplace approval.

_published_faq.name: How clear is Celesto Cloud Computers's MCP tool documentation?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 15, 2026, Celesto Cloud Computers scores 94/100 in Manufact's review of tool titles, descriptions, input and output schemas, and behavior annotations. The review covers 10 of 10 discovered tools. The quality score measures documentation clarity; runtime behavior and marketplace readiness require separate checks.

_published_faq.name: What are the best alternatives to Celesto Cloud Computers?

acceptedAnswer.text: As of October 17, 2026, alternatives to Celesto Cloud Computers in developer-tools on the Manufact MCP catalog include Held at the Gate, Speko, turva.dev, AgentMail, and GitCafe.
